references.text: A parallel law in Leviticus describing the same criteria for clean animals: split hooves and chewing the cud.
The complete parallel text in Leviticus about which land animals are clean and unclean to eat, with the same criteria regarding split hooves and chewing the cud.
An earlier law stating that Israel shall be a holy people, which is the basis for the dietary rules concerning clean and unclean animals.
The immediate context listing specific examples of animals that meet these criteria: ox, sheep, goat, deer, roe deer, etc.
Peter's vision where God declares all animals clean, showing the fulfillment and abolition of these Old Testament dietary laws in the new covenant.
